title: The four quadrants of the Cartesian coordinate plane
competency: Describe the Cartesian plane, locate points from their coordinates and name their quadrant.

keywords.def: The plane made by a horizontal and a vertical number line that cross at right angles.
The point where the x-axis and y-axis meet: (0, 0).
The pair (a, b) that gives a point: a across, then b up or down.
One of the four parts the axes cut the plane into.

en.text: Draw a horizontal number line and a vertical one through its 0. Together they make the Cartesian coordinate plane. The horizontal line is the x-axis. The vertical line is the y-axis. They meet at the origin, (0, 0).

screens.title: Find a seat
screens.ask: In a hall, a seat is found by its row and its number. How many numbers find a point on a flat page?
screens.after: Two numbers: how far across, and how far up or down. This is the idea of the coordinate plane.

screens.title: Definition 3.12
paras: Two number lines cross at right angles. Together they make the Cartesian coordinate plane.
The horizontal number line is called the x-axis.
The vertical number line is called the y-axis.
The point where the two axes meet is called the origin.

points.name: O
points.info: The origin: the x-axis and the y-axis meet here.

screens.title: Key words
defs: The plane made by a horizontal and a vertical number line that cross at right angles.
The point where the x-axis and y-axis meet: (0, 0).

screens.text: Name the axis: the horizontal number line is called the:
screens.why:
Horizontal means across, from left to right.
The horizontal number line is the x-axis.
The vertical one is the y-axis.
The origin is the point where they meet.

screens.ask: Name the point: the place where the x-axis and the y-axis meet is called the ___.
screens.why:
The two axes cross at one point.
That point is called the origin.
Its coordinates are (0, 0).
screens.clue: It is where you start counting.

screens.text: The y-axis: true or false? On the y-axis, positive numbers are above 0.
screens.why:
The y-axis is vertical.
Numbers grow as you go up.
So positive numbers are above 0 and negatives below. True.
screens.clue: Which way do numbers grow on the y-axis?

screens.text: Points with x = 0: where is every point whose x-coordinate is 0?
screens.why:
x = 0 means no move left or right.
You only move up or down from the origin.
So you stay on the y-axis, like (0, 3) or (0, −2).
Not only the origin: y can be any number.
screens.clue: Start at the origin. Do not move left or right.

en.text: A point is written (a, b). The first number a is the x-coordinate: move right if positive, left if negative. The second number b is the y-coordinate: move up if positive, down if negative. (3, 2) is 3 right and 2 up.

screens.title: Which move first?
screens.ask: To reach (3, 2) from the origin, which move comes first?
screens.after: The first number tells the move across. Go 3 right, then 2 up.

screens.title: Locating points on the coordinate plane
paras: A point is described by two numbers (a, b), called coordinates.
The first number a is the x-coordinate (abscissa).
The second number b is the y-coordinate (ordinate).

screens.title: To locate a point (a, b)
screens.ask: To locate a point (a, b), tap each step.
items: Right if a is positive, left if a is negative.
Up if b is positive, down if b is negative.

screens.title: Locate (−3, 2)
steps: x-coordinate −3: move 3 units left from the origin.

screens.title: Note
paras: Every point on the x-axis has the form (a, 0).
Every point on the y-axis has the form (0, b).

screens.title: Key words
defs: The pair (a, b) that gives a point: a across, then b up or down.

screens.text: Locating points: how do you locate (−3, 2)?
screens.why:
The first number is across: −3 means 3 units left.
The second number is up or down: 2 means 2 up.
So go 3 left, then 2 up.
"2 left, then 3 up" swaps the numbers.

screens.text: Write the coordinates: point C is 3 units right and 4 units down from the origin. C = ?
screens.why:
Right 3 gives x = 3.
Down 4 gives y = −4.
Write x first: (3, −4).
(−4, 3) puts the numbers in the wrong order.
screens.clue: Across first, then up or down.

screens.ask: Write the coordinates: start at the origin and move 5 units left. Do not move up or down. The point is (___, 0).
screens.why:
Left means negative.
5 units left: x = −5.
No move up or down: y = 0.
The point is (−5, 0), on the x-axis.

screens.text: Write the coordinates: point F sits on the y-axis, 1 unit below the origin. F = ?
screens.why:
On the y-axis, x = 0.
Below the origin means negative: y = −1.
So F = (0, −1).
(−1, 0) is on the x-axis instead.
screens.clue: On the y-axis, what is x?

screens.why:
Start at the origin (0, 0).
x = 3: go 3 units right.
y = −4: then go 4 units down.
Mark the point there: C(3, −4).
screens.clue: The first number moves you left or right. The second moves you up or down.

screens.ask: Plot two points: B(−3, 4) and E(−1, 0).
screens.why:
B(−3, 4): start at the origin, go 3 left, then 4 up.
E(−1, 0): go 1 left.
y = 0, so do not move up or down.
E is on the x-axis.
screens.clue: Negative x means go left. A y of 0 means stay on the x-axis.

screens.text: Moving a point: start at (2, −1). Move 3 units left and 4 units up. Where are you?
screens.why:
Left 3 changes x: 2 − 3 = −1.
Up 4 changes y: −1 + 4 = 3.
You are at (−1, 3).
(5, 3) moves right instead of left.
screens.clue: Change x for left/right and y for up/down.

en.text: The axes cut the plane into four quadrants. Quadrant I is (+, +). Quadrant II is (−, +). Quadrant III is (−, −). Quadrant IV is (+, −). A point with a 0 coordinate lies on an axis, not in a quadrant.

screens.title: Both positive
screens.ask: In which part of the plane are both coordinates positive?
screens.after: Right means x positive and up means y positive. That is the upper right: Quadrant I.

screens.title: Quadrants
screens.ask: The x-axis and the y-axis divide the plane into 4 regions called quadrants. Tap each one.

points.name: N
points.info: x = 0: on the y-axis, in no quadrant.

points.name: P
points.info: y = 0: on the x-axis, in no quadrant.

screens.title: Key words
defs: One of the four parts the axes cut the plane into.

screens.why:
Look at the signs.
x = −4 is negative. y = 1 is positive.
(−, +) is Quadrant II: the upper left.

Look at the sign of each coordinate.
(4, 1) is (+, +): Quadrant I.
(−3, −3) is (−, −): Quadrant III.
(1, −3) is (+, −): Quadrant IV.
(0, 9) and (−3, 0) have a 0, so they lie on an axis.
screens.clue: Write the signs (+ or −) of x and y.
screens.text: Sort each point: which quadrant, or on an axis?
Which quadrant? Where is the point (−7/4, −13/5)?
screens.why:
−7/4 is negative, so x < 0.
−13/5 is negative, so y < 0.
(−, −) is Quadrant III.
Fractions do not change the sign rule.
screens.clue: Fractions do not change the rule. Look at the signs.

screens.ask: Plot a point in Quadrant III: tap (−2, −4).
screens.why:
Start at the origin.
x = −2: go 2 units left.
y = −4: go 4 units down.
Both are negative: (−, −) is Quadrant III.

screens.text: Signs of coordinates: a is negative and b is positive. Where is the point (b, a)?
screens.why:
In (b, a), the x-coordinate is b.
b is positive, so x > 0.
The y-coordinate is a, which is negative.
(+, −) is Quadrant IV.
Quadrant II would be the point (a, b).

screens.title: The number line
steps: 0 is in the middle of the number line.
Positive numbers go to the right: 1, 2, 3, …
Negative numbers go to the left: −1, −2, −3, …

screens.text: Integers on a number line: where is −3?
screens.why:
Negative numbers are to the left of 0.
−3 is 3 steps from 0.
So −3 is 3 units left of 0.
+3 would be 3 units right.
screens.clue: Which side are negative numbers on?

items.why:
x = −1 is negative: 1 left.
y = 4 is positive: 4 up.
(−, +) is Quadrant II.

x = −3: 3 left.
y = −2: 2 down.
(−, −) is Quadrant III.

items.text: On an axis? Where is R(0, −3)?
items.why:
x = 0, so there is no move left or right.
y = −3: 3 down.
The point is on the y-axis, below the origin.
It is not in Quadrant IV: a point on an axis is in no quadrant.

x = 3/2 = 1.5 is positive: right.
y = −5 is negative: down.
(+, −) is Quadrant IV.

items.text: Read the figure: T is 3 units left and 3 units down. T = ?
Read the figure: M is 2 units right and 4 units down. M = ?
items.why:
Right 2: x = 2.
Down 4: y = −4.
Write x first: M = (2, −4).

items.text: Read the figure: Q is 2 left and 3 up; N is on the y-axis at 4. Which point has coordinates (−2, 3)?
items.why:
(−2, 3): x = −2 means 2 left.
y = 3 means 3 up.
Q is 2 left and 3 up.
So the point is Q.

items.text: Which quadrant? Where is the point (−3, 27)?
items.why:
x = −3 is negative.
y = 27 is positive.
(−, +) is Quadrant II.

items.text: On an axis? Where is the point (5/2, 0)?
items.why:
y = 0, so there is no move up or down.
x = 5/2 = 2.5: right of the origin.
The point is on the x-axis.

items.text: Which quadrant? Where is the point (35, −12.5)?
items.why:
x = 35 is positive.
y = −12.5 is negative.
(+, −) is Quadrant IV.

test.text: Name the axis: the vertical number line is called the:
test.why:
Vertical means up and down.
The vertical number line is the y-axis.
The horizontal one is the x-axis.

x = 4 is positive.
y = 1 is positive.
(+, +) is Quadrant I.

test.text: On an axis: which point lies on the x-axis?
test.why:
Every point on the x-axis has y = 0.
(−3, 0) has y = 0.
(0, 9) has x = 0: it is on the y-axis.
(1, −3) is in Quadrant IV.

test.text: Write the coordinates: a point is 4 units left and 2 units up from the origin. It is:
test.why:
Left 4: x = −4.
Up 2: y = 2.
The point is (−4, 2).

test.text: Moving a point: start at (−2, 3) and move 5 units right. In which quadrant are you now?
test.why:
Moving right changes x: −2 + 5 = 3.
y stays 3.
The new point is (3, 3).
(+, +) is Quadrant I.
